body: A classroom light was often left on after the last lesson. The class first decided that the student nearest the door always turned it off. This worked on some days. It failed after an early exit for club activities. The class checked its schedule and found that different students were last in the room on different days. They placed a small check card beside the door. The last person leaving turned off the light and moved the card from “on” to “checked.” For two weeks, the light was not left on once. A task connected to the last person worked well. A task connected to one fixed student did not.
prompt: Complete the summary: The class replaced a rule based on one student's seat with a rule based on ____.
evidence: The class checked its schedule and found that different students were last in the room on different days. The last person leaving turned off the light and moved the card from “on” to “checked.”
evidenceJp: 予定を確認すると、最後まで教室にいる生徒は日によって違うことが分かりました。そこでドアのそばに小さな確認カードを置きました。最後に出る人が電気を消し、カードを「点灯中」から「確認済み」へ動かします。
answer: who was last to leave the room
reason: The new responsibility follows the actual last person rather than a fixed student.

body: After music class, Ren found a small note under a music stand. It said, ‘Practice in Room 3 at four.’ There were two school bands, so Ren did not know the right group for the note. He looked at the room schedule on the wall. The brass band used Room 3 at four, and the guitar club used it at five. Ren carried the note to the brass band teacher. The teacher thanked him and put the note on the band's board. Ren did not guess from the room alone. He checked the time too, and that helped him choose the right group.
prompt: 9. メモと部屋予定表を合わせると何が分かりましたか。
evidence: It said, ‘Practice in Room 3 at four.’ / The brass band used Room 3 at four, and the guitar club used it at five.
evidenceJp: そこには「4時に第3室で練習」と書かれていました。 / 吹奏楽部は4時に第3室を使い、ギター部は5時に使うことが分かりました。
answer: 4時の第3室は吹奏楽部なので、メモは吹奏楽部向けだと分かった。
reason: 時間と場所を照合して届け先を特定しています。

body: Haru's class grew three kinds of plants by the classroom window. On Friday, one name marker fell out of a pot. Haru found the marker on the floor, but the right pot was not clear. He looked at the planting map in the class notebook. The middle pot had the word ‘basil.’ Then he compared the leaves with a picture from Monday. The middle plant had the same round leaves as the basil in the picture. Haru put the marker into that pot. He showed the map and the picture to his teacher. The teacher said, “Good check.”
prompt: 9. 植え付け図と葉の写真を合わせると何が分かりましたか。
evidence: The middle pot had the word ‘basil.’ / The middle plant had the same round leaves as the basil in the picture.
evidenceJp: 真ん中の鉢には「バジル」という言葉がありました。 / 真ん中の植物には写真のバジルと同じ丸い葉がありました。
answer: 真ん中の鉢がバジルである可能性が高いと分かった。
reason: 位置と見た目の両方が一致しています。

body: The teacher said to Riku, “Please give out these English worksheets.” He found two piles on the teacher's desk. The first pile started on page 32, but the second started on page 34. Both had the same lesson title. Riku almost mixed the piles together. Then he looked at the board. On the board, he saw, ‘Today: pages 32-33. Next class: pages 34-35.’ Riku gave his classmates the first pile and left the second pile on the desk. The teacher came in and said, “Thank you for checking.” A small page number stopped a simple mistake.
prompt: 9. プリントの開始ページと黒板の情報を合わせると何が分かりましたか。
evidence: The first pile started on page 32, but the second started on page 34. / On the board, he saw, ‘Today: pages 32-33. Next class: pages 34-35.’
evidenceJp: 一つ目は32ページから、二つ目は34ページから始まっていました。 / 黒板には「今日：32〜33ページ。次の授業：34〜35ページ」とありました。
answer: 32ページからの束が今日用、34ページからの束が次回用だと分かった。
reason: 二つの情報が対応します。

body: Shun carried old paper to the recycling corner. One box had two arrows on its side. A blue arrow pointed to a narrow opening, and a gray arrow pointed to a larger opening. Shun first thought both openings were for paper. He read the words under the arrows. The blue side said ‘flat paper,’ and the gray side said ‘paper cups.’ His papers were flat worksheets, so he used the blue opening. Later, a teacher said, “Paper cups need a different process.” Shun was glad. He read the words and did not use the larger opening only for its size.
prompt: 6. この話の中心内容として最も適切なものはどれですか。
evidence: He read the words under the arrows. / His papers were flat worksheets, so he used the blue opening.
evidenceJp: しかし矢印の下の言葉を読むと、青い側には「平らな紙」、灰色の側には「紙コップ」と書かれていました。持っていたのは平らなプリントだったので、青い投入口を使いました。
answer: B. 表示を読んで正しい分別方法を選んだ話
reason: 表示確認によって正しい投入口を選ぶことが話の中心です。

evidence: His papers were flat worksheets, so he used the blue opening. / Shun was glad.
evidenceJp: 持っていたのは平らなプリントだったので、青い投入口を使いました。 / シュンはよかったと思いました。
answer: 表示を読んで、持っていた平らなプリントを正しい投入口に入れられたから。
reason: 正しい分別ができた直後に安心しているためです。

body: Kenta was helping with a small book display in the library. On Wednesday, he saw one display book on the normal shelf. He thought, “Is the display over?” and started to move the other books too. Then he checked the card beside the display. It said the display would continue until Friday. Kenta also looked at the return slip inside the missing book. A student borrowed it before the display began and returned it that morning. Kenta showed the slip to the librarian before he moved the book. She checked the date and said, “The student made a mistake.” The student did not know that the book now belonged on the special table. Kenta told the librarian, and they put the book back on the display. He left the other books where they were. Checking both the event card and the return slip showed him why one book had moved early.
prompt: 9. 展示カードと返却票を合わせると何が分かりましたか。
evidence: It said the display would continue until Friday. / A student borrowed it before the display began and returned it that morning.
evidenceJp: 金曜日まで続くと書かれていました。 / ある生徒が展示開始前に借り、今朝返したことが分かりました。
answer: 展示は続いており、その本だけが返却時の間違いで普通棚に置かれたと分かった。
reason: 展示期間と返却履歴を合わせて原因を説明できます。

body: Hina found a name card on the floor near the classroom sink. The printed name was wet, and she read only the first letter, M. Three students in the class had names beginning with M. Hina looked at the seating chart, but that did not show the card’s owner. Then she remembered the class photo on the wall. In the photo, one student had the same green star on her name card. Hina checked the star and returned the card to Miki. Miki smiled and said she had dropped it while washing her hands.
prompt: In this passage, what does 'owner' mean?
evidence: The seating chart did not show the card’s owner.
evidenceJp: 座席表だけでは誰が名札をなくしたのか分かりませんでした。
answer: The person the name card belongs to.
reason: The owner is the student whose name card it is.

body: Ken practiced the piano for thirty minutes every evening. He wanted to improve a difficult part of one song, but he often made the same mistakes near the end of practice. He thought he needed to practice longer. His teacher said, “Try the difficult part first for one week.” Ken kept the total practice time at thirty minutes. In the morning on Saturday, he also tried the same part before breakfast. He noticed fewer mistakes on days he was not tired. He changed the order of his evening practice and continued to work on the difficult part first. The change helped without adding more practice time.
prompt: What does “the same part” refer to?
evidence: Try the difficult part first... he also tried the same part
evidenceJp: 「同じ部分」は曲の難しい部分を指します。
answer: The difficult part of the song.
reason: The phrase refers back to the teacher's suggested target.

body: At the school festival, two food stands sold different snacks. Visitors kept choosing Stand B because its line looked shorter. However, some of them later said they had waited longer there. The festival team wanted to know why. They counted people in each line every five minutes and also measured the time from ordering to receiving food. Stand A usually had twelve people waiting, but each order took about forty seconds. Stand B often had only seven people, yet each order took nearly ninety seconds because one snack had to be heated after the order. The team put a small sign at both stands showing the usual preparation time. They also prepared part of Stand B's snack before the busiest period. Visitors could then choose with better information, and the longest waits became shorter. Line length alone had hidden the real cause. The team checked again during the final hour to see whether the change only worked once. Stand B still had fewer people in line than Stand A, but its waiting time was now close to the time shown on the sign. The second check supported their explanation.
prompt: 1. この話の中心内容として最も適切なものはどれですか。
evidence: They counted people in each line every five minutes and also measured the time from ordering to receiving food. / The team put a small sign at both stands showing the usual preparation time. They also prepared part of Stand B's snack before the busiest period.
evidenceJp: 5分ごとに各列の人数を数え、注文してから受け取るまでの時間も測りました。 / チームは両方の店に、通常の調理時間を示す小さな表示を置きました。また、混雑する時間の前にB店の調理の一部を準備しました。
answer: B. 待ち時間の原因を調べ、表示と準備方法を改善した話
reason: 列の人数だけでなく実際の処理時間を測り、その結果を使って改善したことが話の中心です。

body: The student council made a survey about the school festival. Its first question asked students to choose among five detailed plans for next year. When six first-year students tested the form, three stopped at that question. They said they did not know enough about the plans. The survey team discussed the result and kept the useful question but moved it later. The new first question was simple: ‘Which part of this year's festival did you use or visit?’ Later questions gave short information before asking about future choices. In a second test, all six students reached the end. Changing the order did not remove important thinking. It gave students information and confidence before the hardest question.
prompt: 7. 最初のテストと2回目のテストの結果を合わせると、何が分かりますか。
evidence: When six first-year students tested the form, three stopped at that question. / In a second test, all six students reached the end.
evidenceJp: 1年生6人に試してもらうと、3人がその質問で止まりました。 / 2回目のテストでは6人全員が最後まで答えました。
answer: A. 順番と情報提示の変更が回答しやすさを改善した
reason: 改善前後の結果比較から効果を判断できます。

evidenceJp: 順番を変えたことは、大切な思考をなくしたのではありません。 / 後の質問では短い情報を示してから、将来の選択を尋ねました。

reason: 内容を消したのではなく、回答に必要な準備を先に置いています。

body: A sports center sometimes closed its outdoor court after heavy rain. Staff posted closure notices on a board inside the building, but some students still walked twenty minutes to the center before learning that practice was canceled. The staff thought the notice itself was clear. A youth group mapped when players needed the information. They found that most decided whether to leave home about thirty minutes before practice. The center began posting the same notice on its website as soon as a decision was made and kept the indoor board as well. The number of unnecessary trips went down. Good information was not enough when it reached people after they had already acted.
prompt: In “as soon as a decision was made,” what decision is meant?
evidence: A sports center sometimes closed its outdoor court after heavy rain. The center began posting the same notice on its website as soon as a decision was made and kept the indoor board as well.
evidenceJp: スポーツセンターでは、大雨の後に屋外コートを閉鎖することがありました。そこでセンターは、決定したらすぐウェブサイトにも同じ案内を出し、館内の掲示も残しました。
answer: The decision to close the outdoor court and cancel practice there.
reason: The notice concerns whether the rain has caused the court closure.

body: A reading group met every Wednesday. Students discussed one story, but two confident members usually spoke first and for a long time. The teacher noticed that quieter students often had written good notes but rarely shared them. Instead of setting a strict speaking limit for everyone, the group tried a new opening rule. For the first five minutes, each person chose one sentence from the story and explained why it mattered. After everyone had spoken once, the discussion became free. More students joined the later conversation because they had already entered it with one idea. The rule did not reduce strong opinions; it created a fair starting point for them.
prompt: Why might a strict speaking limit for the whole discussion have been less suitable?
evidence: After everyone had spoken once, the discussion became free. The rule did not reduce strong opinions; it created a fair starting point for them.
evidenceJp: 全員が一度話した後は自由な話し合いにしました。このルールは強い意見を減らしたのではなく、全員に公平な出発点を作りました。
answer: The group wanted broad participation while still allowing strong ideas and free discussion after everyone had entered the conversation.
reason: The final design balanced equal entry with open discussion rather than controlling every turn.

body: The art club made a poster for its open room. They placed it low on a wall near the stairs because the colors looked bright there. During lunch, however, few students entered. Yuto stood in the crowded hallway to see why. Bags and students blocked the lower wall, and he could not read the club name from several meters away. The members tested the same poster in two higher places. They asked ten students to walk from the stairs and say when they noticed it. More students saw it early when it was at eye level near the corner. The club moved the poster there instead of printing a larger one. The next day, more visitors found the room.
prompt: 7. 最初の掲示場所を決めたとき、美術部が十分に考えていなかった点は何ですか。
evidence: They placed it low on a wall near the stairs because the colors looked bright there. / Bags and students blocked the lower wall, and he could not read the club name from several meters away.
evidenceJp: 色が明るく見えるので、階段近くの壁の低い位置に貼りました。 / ユウトが混んだ廊下に立って理由を確かめると、かばんや生徒が壁の下の部分を隠し、数メートル離れると部名を読めませんでした。
answer: 混雑した廊下で実際に生徒からポスターが見えるかどうか。
reason: 色の見え方を重視した一方、実際の通行状況での視認性を確認していませんでした。

body: Visitors often stopped at the campus map near the front gate and then walked in the wrong direction. The map was correct, so volunteers first planned to add arrows. Sora watched five visitors use it. The top of the map showed north, but people at the gate were facing south. Some turned left on the paper and then turned left with their bodies, although those directions were different. The team printed a test copy rotated to match the view from the gate. They asked five more visitors to find the science room. Four chose the correct path without help. The team kept a small north mark but used the visitor's view as the main direction. Rotating the map worked better than adding many arrows.
prompt: 1. この話の中心内容として最も適切なものはどれですか。
evidence: The team printed a test copy rotated to match the view from the gate. / Rotating the map worked better than adding many arrows.
evidenceJp: 班は、門から見える向きに合わせて回転させた試作地図を印刷しました。 / 矢印を増やすより、地図を回転させる方が効果的でした。
answer: B. 来校者の向きに合わせて地図を回転させ、道案内を改善した話
reason: 利用者の視点に地図の向きを合わせる改善が話の中心です。

body: Teachers received reports that some students could not hear the afternoon announcement. It sounded clear in the office, so the cause was not obvious. A student team tested the message in the library, at the east stairs, and in the old music hall. They wrote down which words they missed. The first two places were fine. In the music hall, the message became very quiet whenever the fire door in the connecting hallway was closed. The speaker was on the other side. The school did not leave the fire door open. It added a speaker inside the hall and repeated the test with the door closed. All three listeners then heard the complete message. The solution kept the safety rule and fixed the problem.
prompt: 5. 学校が防火扉を開けたままにしなかった理由として最も適切なものはどれですか。
evidence: The school did not leave the fire door open. / The solution kept the safety rule and fixed the problem.
evidenceJp: 学校は防火扉を開けたままにはせず、 / 安全の決まりを守りながら、連絡の問題を解決しました。
answer: A. 安全上の決まりを守る必要があったから
reason: 安全を崩さず設備側を改善したことから判断できます。

body: An exchange group prepared a Japanese guide for visiting students. One English page had been translated into very formal Japanese, and local students said it sounded polite. However, two visiting students still asked what they should do after arriving at the meeting point. The group compared the English and Japanese versions line by line. The Japanese text described the place correctly but hid the action inside a long sentence. They rewrote it as two short instructions: meet at the east gate and show your name card to a helper. Nothing important was removed. The new version was easier to follow because the action appeared clearly and in the order visitors needed it.
prompt: Why did the group not simply add more information to the Japanese guide?
evidence: The Japanese text described the place correctly but hid the action inside a long sentence. Nothing important was removed.
evidenceJp: 日本語は場所を正しく説明していましたが、行動の指示が長い文の中に隠れていました。大切な情報は削っていません。
answer: The needed information was already present; the problem was that the actions were hidden and poorly ordered.
reason: The rewrite improved structure and clarity rather than content quantity.

body: Students were preparing cakes for a charity café. Their recipe used 200 milliliters of milk for one cake, and they expected to sell eighteen cakes. A simple calculation suggested 3.6 liters of milk. One student proposed buying exactly that amount to avoid waste. Another pointed out that the new oven had never been used for this recipe. The group baked one test cake first and found that the oven dried the cake slightly, so they increased the milk to 220 milliliters for each later cake. They also decided to prepare only twelve cakes before opening and make more if sales were strong. The first twelve sold quickly, so they made six more. Because the group tested both the recipe and the demand before committing everything, it bought enough milk without producing many unsold cakes. The small test changed two assumptions that the original calculation could not check.
prompt: Why was buying exactly 3.6 liters at the beginning risky?
evidence: Another pointed out that the new oven had never been used for this recipe... They also decided to prepare only twelve cakes before opening and make more if sales were strong.
evidenceJp: 新しいオーブンでは未試験で、販売数も実際の売れ行きを見て追加することにしました。
answer: The recipe amount and expected demand had not yet been tested under actual conditions.
reason: 計算自体は正しいが、牛乳量と需要の前提が未検証だった。

body: A junior high school planned a winter community event for seventy-two students, eight teachers, and eighteen guests. The original plan used an outdoor plaza from ten in the morning until three in the afternoon. Two days before the event, the forecast changed to light snow at nine, possible heavy snow at noon, and stronger wind by three. The organizers agreed that umbrellas alone would not solve travel and exposure risks. They looked at three indoor venues instead of canceling immediately. The Civic Hall held one hundred twenty people but was available only until two thirty. The Sports Center held eighty and stayed open until five, while the Library Room held only thirty-five. The total group was ninety-eight, so the Civic Hall was the only single room large enough for everyone. The first indoor draft still ended at three, after the hall closed. The organizers shortened shared activities to finish at one forty-five. That left forty-five minutes for coats, attendance checks, and organized departure. Transport created another problem: two school buses had forty-five seats each, only ninety in total. The organizers checked registration forms instead of assuming who could arrange private transport. Twelve students lived near the hall and had previous permission to meet there directly in normal weather. Because snow was now forecast, the school contacted those families again. Seven families chose direct transport, while five requested bus seats because roads might become slippery. That still left ninety-one people needing seats, one more than the buses could carry. A school van with eight passenger seats was available and approved for staff travel. The transport office confirmed a licensed staff driver and winter tires. The final plan used both buses plus the van, with assigned passenger lists. Families received departure times, vehicle assignments, and a morning contact number. The school set a six thirty weather check and a cancellation rule for severe road warnings. On event day, snow stayed light in the morning, so the group used the revised plan and finished before conditions worsened. body: A school festival committee had to place three activities into two rooms and the main hall. Room A held 30 people, Room B held 45, and the hall held 90. A craft workshop expected 28 participants and needed tables. A music performance expected 70 and needed a stage. A short science show expected 40 but used equipment that had to stay indoors. The first plan put the craft workshop in Room A, science in Room B, and music in the hall. Then the committee learned that Room B would be unavailable from 1:00 to 1:40 for an electrical inspection. The science show was scheduled for 1:20. Rather than moving every event, the committee shifted the science show to 2:00, kept its room, and used the inspection period as setup time. The craft and music schedules remained unchanged. By separating a room-capacity problem from a time-availability problem, the committee found a small adjustment instead of rebuilding the whole plan.

body: Students helped prepare an emergency guide for an international exchange event. The first draft told everyone to gather “behind the gym” after an earthquake. Local students knew that this meant the open field on the north side, but visiting students who read the English guide could not tell which side was meant. During a practice drill, two visitors walked toward a narrow service road south of the gym. The safety team stopped the drill and compared the Japanese map, the English guide, and the signs outside. They changed the instruction to “Go to the north field behind the gym” and added an arrow from the main entrance. They also placed the same English words on the outdoor sign. The drill was repeated, and all groups reached the correct field. The original instruction had seemed obvious only because local students shared knowledge that visitors did not have.
